changes.old: It is optional for police agencies to report to the FBI. Some agencies report every month, some report a few months, and some don't report at all. Coverage is the share of a metro's people living in areas whose agencies reported a full year. These shares are based on the reported crimes only in the population those agencies cover, not the whole metro, so cities where many agencies don't report to the FBI will not have rates that appear artificially low. When coverage becomes too sparse, no figure is shown at all on this site.
changes.new: (none)

changes.where: docs/crime.md, section "Why cities aren't compared on crime"
changes.old: Crime figures collected by different cities may have different reporting habits and cover different shares of their people, making cross-city comparisons potentially misleading. This is why the FBI cautions against using their data to rank or compare cities. The crime figures on city pages are provided as context, but not used in the calculations of any of this site's scores.
changes.new: Crime figures collected by different cities may have different reporting habits and cover different shares of their people, making cross-city comparisons potentially misleading. It is optional for police agencies to report to the FBI. Some agencies report every month, some report a few months, and some don't report at all. This is why the FBI cautions against using their data to rank or compare cities. The crime figures on city pages are provided as context, but not used in the calculations of any of this site's scores. The numbers on this site are based on the crimes in geographic regions covered by reporting agencies, not whole metros, so cities where many agencies don't report to the FBI will not have rates that appear artificially low. When coverage becomes too sparse, no figure is shown at all on this site.

changes.kind: changed (Nathan's copy, its last clause rephrased at his request on 2026-10-07: "what you select stays in your browser" read as if the search never left the browser, while the next section says it travels to the server)
changes.old: **In short:** you don't sign up, we don't track you, and what you tell us about yourself stays in your browser.
changes.new: There is no account needed to use this site, we don't track you, and we don't save your searches.

changes.old: The people you're looking for — their sex, ages, marital status, education, income and race or ethnicity — and your own age travel to our server so it can build the page you asked for. We use them for that and nothing else, and we don't save them on our servers.
changes.new: The people you're looking for (e.g. sex, age, marital status, education, income, and race or ethnicity) and your own age travel to our server so it can provide the information on matches that you're interested in. We use them for that and nothing else, and we don't save those searches on our servers. Your own browser will keep details about you so the site remembers them for the next time you visit. You can remove them at any time by clearing this site's data in your browser's settings.

changes.old: Your own sex, your education and your race or ethnicity stay in your browser. They are never sent to us: not in a web address, a request, a cookie or any other way. Our server works out the figures for every possible answer, and your browser shows the ones that fit you. Your race or ethnicity is used only if you include it. Your browser keeps these details so the site remembers them next time. You can remove them at any time by clearing this site's data in your browser's settings.
changes.new: (none)

changes.old: One cookie, called dsa_prefs, remembers the rest of your search — the people you're looking for and your age, never your own sex, education or race — for up to 30 days, so the site can show your search again when you come back. You can delete it at any time in your browser's settings.
changes.new: One cookie, called dsa_prefs, remembers the rest of your search, the people you're looking for and your age, for up to 30 days, so the site can show your search again when you come back. You can delete it at any time in your browser's settings.

changes.old: The site runs on a server we rent from Oracle Cloud. The server keeps no record of your visits — not your IP address, and not the pages you look at. Oracle's network carries traffic to and from it, and like any network it sees IP addresses, under Oracle's own privacy policy.
changes.new: The site runs on a server we rent from Oracle Cloud. The server keeps no record of your visits, not your IP address, and not the pages you look at. Oracle's network carries traffic to and from it, and like any network it sees IP addresses, under Oracle's own privacy policy.

changes.old: The race and sex details on this site are used only to work out the figures on the page you asked for. They never feed advertising, listings, referrals, or any housing, credit or job use.

changes.where: docs/terms.md, section "Estimates, not facts about people"
changes.old: - Every figure is an estimate. The counts come from the Census Bureau's household survey, which samples households, so every figure carries some uncertainty. Where the sample is too thin to trust, the site leaves the city out rather than show a number; About us explains how the figures are made. - The compatibility figure describes a pattern across many real couples. It says nothing about any one person. - The figures are Dating Stats Atlas's own estimates from Census Bureau and other public data. No government agency made, checked or endorses them. - We work to keep the figures accurate, but we can't promise they are complete, current or right for your situation, and none of them is advice. Check anything that matters to you, such as where to live, against other sources.
